t: Muhammad posted 50 archers on a hill to guard the Muslim rear against the Meccan cavalry; when most of them went down to join the advance, Khalid ibn al-Walid's cavalry attacked the flank and rear.
Ibn al-Athir names 85 Muslims killed, 75 of them Medinans and 10 Emigrants from Mecca.
Chase F. Robinson calls the Muslim defeat clear enough, while William Montgomery Watt notes that the Meccans failed to achieve their aim of destroying Muhammad and his followers.
dyk: Abu Sufyan shouted from the mountain that victory in war goes by turns and that this day was in exchange for the day of Badr, and Umar ibn al-Khattab answered him by Muhammad's instruction.
ev: The Quraysh are defeated at Badr and several of their leaders are killed, among them Amr ibn Hisham
Abu Sufyan mobilises a force of over 3,000 men to retaliate for the losses at Badr
Muhammad yields to those who want to fight in the open, and the Muslims take position on the slopes of Uhud; Abd Allah ibn Ubayy withdraws with 300 men
Duels between standard-bearers open the fighting and the Meccan lines are pushed back
Most of the archers leave the hill, and Khalid ibn al-Walid's cavalry attacks the Muslim flank and rear; Hamza is killed
Umar leads a counter-charge that dislodges Khalid's forces from the slopes, and the fighting ceases
The Meccans halt at Hamra al-Asad, and Muhammad sends out a small force to scout them
Abu Sufyan and allied tribes attack Medina in the Battle of the Trench

f.place: A valley north of Medina near Mount Uhud, in present-day Saudi Arabia
f.sides: The Quraysh of Mecca under Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, with a force of approximately 3,000 men, 700 of them in chain mail; the early Muslims under Muhammad, 1,000 men at first and around 700 after 300 withdrew, of whom 100 had chain mail
f.outcome: The Muslims suffered heavy losses, among them Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and the Meccans withdrew without pressing home their advantage; scholars differ on whether this was a Muslim defeat or an indecisive result.
